• Saint Martin is celebrated on 11 November and on 4 July (the date he was raised to bishop, in 371).

• A short biography of an ascetic hierarch:

• Saint Martin is one of the most popular saints in the Catholic Church, and he is also venerated as a saint in the Orthodox Church.
Saint Martin was born around the year 316 in Savaria (in the province of Pannonia, today Szombathely in Hungary), the son of a pagan Roman tribune, but he received a Christian education in Pavia, his father's home town, becoming a catechumen at the age of ten.
Obeying his father, he had to enlist in the Roman imperial army, serving in the bodyguard of Emperor Constantius II. Posted to the cavalry legions at Amiens (in Gaul), he once met a nearly naked beggar at the city gate. Moved with pity, he cut his cloak (called “cappa” in Latin) in two with his sword and gave half of it to the man in need. The following night he dreamt of the Lord Christ, who revealed to him that He Himself had been present in the form of the poor man.

3e9829182551:
«The Coronation of the Mother of God» is an iconographic theme found very often in the wall paintings of Orthodox churches, in icons on glass and in the religious paintings of the great Western painters of the Middle Ages.

Over time, the scene of the Coronation of the Mother of God has had several versions.
In all of them the coronation takes place in heaven.

One of the first versions, promoted by Western art in the early Middle Ages, shows the Virgin Mary enthroned, crowned only by angels. Later the iconographic scene was enriched and became more complex.

The version we are showing you today is painted on glass after a model from Șcheii Brașovului, 19th century.
The icon shows the scene of the Coronation of the Virgin Mary.

Jesus Christ and God the Father sit on suggested thrones and hold the mitre they place on Mary's head.
In the upper register the Holy Spirit appears as a white dove framed by the sun, flanked on each side by two cherubim floating on clouds.
In the lower register, in the middle, Mary kneels, dressed in a red maphorion with a halo on her head and her hands crossed on her chest, with cherubim at her feet.
All the figures are held up by clouds.

The icon is not available; it has gone to Constanța together with «The Eucharistic Jesus» and «The Baptism of the Lord».

f1eaddef6220:
Saint Zoe the Martyr – icon on glass (22x26 cm)

The icon was ordered as a gift for a special lady who celebrates both her birthday and her name day on 18 December

To know part of the life of Saint Zoe, we must also know Saint Sebastian, both being celebrated by the Orthodox Church on 18 December

I found two very different versions of this story. I thought the Romanian Patriarchate was the most reliable source, so I am sharing a short text signed by the Romanian Patriarchate – Pilgrimages department (basilica.ro)

“ Saint Sebastian the Martyr was born in 255 in the city of Narbonne in Gaul (today's France), but grew up in Mediolanum (Milan, Italy), where his family came from. In 283, as the son of a nobleman, he had to join the army of Emperor Carinus (283–285). Sebastian's wish was to help the Christians in their sufferings and troubles.

The opportunity came when two brothers, Marcellinus and Mark, had confessed Christ with great courage and were quietly awaiting death. Their parents, Tranquillinus and Marcia, had asked the judges for 30 days to bring them back to paganism. At this moment of great trial, Sebastian, commander of the first cohort of the Praetorian Guard, came to them. Those present were amazed to hear Sebastian encouraging the two brothers to die for their faith in God: “Soldiers of Christ, see how, through the lifting up of your souls, you have drawn near to victory. Do not deprive yourselves of Him for such useless lamentation… If your parents and brothers knew of eternal life, so full of joy, they would hasten to go with you”

All this happened in the house of Nicostratus, who was in charge of guarding the prisoners. Zoe, the wife of Nicostratus, had been mute for six years. Seeing Sebastian encouraging the two martyrs, she fell on her knees before him, showing him that she was mute. Sebastian made the sign of the cross over her mouth, and at that moment she regained her voice. After this miracle, the martyrs Mark and Marcellinus and their parents Marcia and Tranquillinus, Zoe and her husband Nicostratus, and 16 more of the prisoners received holy baptism from the hands of the presbyter Polycarp

When the persecution of the Christians intensified, Zoe was caught while praying at the tomb of the Holy Apostle Peter and, after five days in prison, suffered a martyr's death. Marcellinus and Mark were tortured and finally received a martyr's death. Saint Sebastian the Martyr died in the hippodrome (the place where horsemen raced), entrusting his soul to God as a martyr”

3d091f8d292c:
The fourth icon of “The Burning Bush of the Theotokos” painted in our workshop

This icon painted on glass is inspired by several depictions, one of them being the first such icon to reach our country (in the 1940s), at the Antim Monastery in Bucharest. Many generations of the Church's servants and of the faithful have prayed before this icon at the Antim Monastery, and it also inspired the well-known hesychast movement “The Burning Bush”, a group that kept the fire of faith alive in the hearts of many Romanians during the communist rule

The icon “The Burning Bush” shows a large eight-pointed star in the form of overlapping rhombuses, with the Mother of God holding the Saviour in her arms at their centre. Four of the eight points are red, representing the fire, and the other four, painted green, symbolise that the bush did not burn but remained whole. On the points of the red star are the symbols of the four Holy Evangelists: the angel (Saint Matthew), the lion (Saint Mark), the ox (Saint Luke) and the eagle (Saint John), and on the four points of the green star the Holy Angels are depicted

This icon is not available; it has already reached Constanța, where it was awaited with great joy

⊹ On Good Friday we are showing you an icon on glass, «The Lamentation of Christ» – model: Șcheii Brașovului, 19th century.

⊹ About the icon:

• The theme of this icon is «the Lamentation of Jesus», after the Descent from the Cross and before the burial itself.

• The icon is one of the rare compositions developed horizontally, as is proper to the epitaphios.

• Its central scene shows the laying of Jesus Christ in the tomb: two apostles hold the shroud at His head and feet, and two angels lift Him from the front. In the background, Mary is surrounded by the holy women and by archangels; seraphim float in the air and (above the cross) the "thrones", angels set in medallions. In the corners of the scene the four Evangelists are shown in medallions. In the upper register, between the medallions and the arch of the vault, two landscapes can be seen: Mount Golgotha on the right and the city of Jerusalem on the left.

⊹ The technique is the traditional one: egg tempera and gold leaf.

⊹ The icon is in the collection of a lovely family from Brașov, so it is not available. If you would like an icon on this theme or any other iconographic theme, contact me and we will settle the details.

In the background, Mary is surrounded by the holy women and by archangels; seraphim float in the air and (above the cross) the "thrones", angels set in medallions. In the corners of the scene the four Evangelists are shown in medallions. In the upper register, between the medallions and the arch of the vault, two landscapes can be seen: Mount Golgotha on the right and the city of Jerusalem on the left.

⊹ The technique is the traditional one: egg tempera and gold leaf.

Obeying his father, he had to enlist in the Roman imperial army, serving in the bodyguard of Emperor Constantius II. Posted to the cavalry legions at Amiens (in Gaul), he once met a nearly naked beggar at the city gate. Moved with pity, he cut his cloak (called “cappa” in Latin) in two with his sword and gave half of it to the man in need. The following night he dreamt of the Lord Christ, who revealed to him that He Himself had been present in the form of the poor man.” (source of the description: doxologia.ro)

❈ On 21 October the Orthodox Church celebrates the Holy Transylvanian Confessors

• We welcome the feast of the Holy Confessors with an icon on glass (30x42 cm) painted in our workshop. The saints depicted in this icon are:

• Visarion Sarai – an Orthodox hieromonk who was imprisoned in the fortress of Kufstein, where he died confessing Orthodoxy

• Sofronie of Cioara – a Romanian monk who led the second anti-Catholic revolt in Transylvania

• Oprea Miclăuș – a Romanian peasant who travelled three times to the imperial Court in Vienna to present the Romanians' wish to remain in the faith of their forefathers. In 1752, together with the priest Moise Măcinic of Sibiel, he was imprisoned at Kufstein, where both departed to the Lord

• Ioan of Galeș – a confessor priest held responsible (by the Habsburg authorities in Transylvania) for coordinating a resistance movement against the Union with Rome; he was finally imprisoned at Kufstein, where he endured 24 years of detention

• Moise Măcinic of Sibiel – a confessor priest who fought against the imposition of the Greek Catholic confession; imprisoned at Kufstein

• The client wished us to depict in this icon also Atanasie Todoran of Bichigiu (celebrated on 12 November), sentenced to death by the imperial power for refusing to renounce the faith of his forefathers, for which he was broken on the wheel at the age of 104

0da107f36000:
~ Icon painted on glass (Saint Cyril and Saint Nicetas) ~
> Orthodox calendar, 18 March 2022. It is a feast day on which Saint Cyril is remembered and his prayer to the Holy Trinity for the enlightenment of the mind and the healing of the body is said!
(I painted the two saints together in an icon ordered for two little brothers.)
> An article by Fr. Ștefan Sfarghie – 18 March 2022:
Saint Cyril (†386) came from the region of Jerusalem and was born in the time of Emperor Constantine the Great (306–337) to Christian parents. He was 12 years old at the time of the First Ecumenical Council of Nicaea, in 325. In those days, the place of Golgotha and the wood of the Holy Cross were being discovered in Jerusalem, and by order of the emperor the Church of the Holy Sepulchre and the Church of the Resurrection were being built. Saint Cyril served in the Church of the Resurrection in his youth, and it was in this church that he delivered his famous Catecheses, or Lectures, preparing for baptism those who wished to become Christians. Around the year 350, when his bishop Maximus died, Saint Cyril was chosen Bishop of the Holy City. The following year the sign of the Holy Cross appeared in the sky over Jerusalem, and the saint informed Emperor Constantius about it in detail. Then hard days began for the Church of Christ, and the Arian emperors Constantius and Valens, together with the Arian bishops, managed twice to remove Saint Cyril, the defender of the apostolic dogmas, from his see. After more than 16 years of exile, towards the end of his life, Saint Cyril returned to his diocese. Shepherding his rational flock with love and leaving the Church the treasure of his 24 Catecheses and the example of his life, he fell asleep in the Lord after taking part in the Second Ecumenical Council of Constantinople in 381.
d8fc76ccdc2c:
Two Saints are depicted in this icon painted on glass: Saint Cyril and Saint Nicetas. Why together? For the simple reason that icons painted on glass are original and special gifts, and this icon was (and is) a special gift for two little brothers.
Happy name day to all who bear the name of Saint Cyril (celebrated today)!

Cyril of Alexandria was Patriarch of Alexandria, a prolific writer and the main protagonist of the Christological controversies of the 4th and 5th centuries. He was the central figure of the Council of Ephesus in 431, which ended with the removal of Nestorius from the see of Archbishop of Constantinople. Saint Cyril is one of the Fathers of the Church, and his fame in the Orthodox world earned him the name “Seal of all the Fathers”.
He is celebrated both on 9 June and on 18 January, together with Saint Athanasius of Alexandria.

Saint Nicetas the Confessor was born in Caesarea of Bithynia, in Asia Minor. As an adult he entered the Monastery of Saint Sergius of Medikion, on Mount Olympus. He was ordained a priest, and in the year 800, after the death of Abbot Nikephoros, Saint Nicetas was made abbot. Under the iconoclast emperor Leo the Armenian (813–820), because of the steadfastness with which he defended the holy icons, Saint Nicetas was imprisoned, subjected to terrible torture and finally confined on the island of Saint Glyceria, in the Sea of Marmara, where he was tormented for six years. After the death of Emperor Leo the Armenian, the persecution of the Christians who venerated the holy icons ceased and the prisoners were freed. Saint Nicetas did not return to his monastery, but joined the community of a hermitage near Constantinople, where he departed to eternal life on 3 April 824. He is celebrated on 3 April, together with Saint Illyricus.
5a0f662078d8:
An icon painted on glass is an object of worship in the Eastern Church and in the Orthodox Christian's home. It can also be a special gift! An unusual gift idea would be the icon of “the Table of Paradise” (which so many of you liked on this page) – a rhombus-shaped table showing the Virgin Mary, the Saviour Jesus Christ and two Saints. Usually the two saints are Saint Nicholas and Saint Paraskeva.

In the icon I am showing you today (as a gift suggestion), Saint George the Great Martyr is painted in the rhombus where Saint Nicholas usually is, and the icon was ordered as a gift for someone special!

Of course, the two saints can be replaced by any other saint (or saints)!
